rules.title: Criminal history screening restrictions - blanket bans and arrest-only records prohibited
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council regulations (effective Jan. 1, 2020)
rules.quote: The California regulations include limits on what type of criminal history may be sought, how an applicant's criminal history can be considered, and what actions a landlord may take based on an applicant's criminal history. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot impose blanket bans on applicants with criminal records and cannot consider arrests without convictions when screening tenants.
rules.effective_date_evidence: which built on the HUD guidance and specifically address the use of criminal history information in housing decisions... rules.title: Source of income discrimination - Section 8 vouchers protected (SB 329)
rules.citation: SB 329 (2019), amending Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quote: In 2019, the California Legislature adopted SB 329, which updated the definition of "source of income" used in the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) to include government housing subsidy programs, such as Section 8. This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.
rules.summary: Landlords are prohibited from refusing to participate in government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.

rules.title: Credit history screening restrictions for voucher holders (SB 267)
rules.citation: SB 267, amending Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quote: last year's SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person's credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot use credit history in screening applicants with government rental subsidies unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay their rent portion.
